topline.text: The big thing to watch this week: Chancellor John Healey delivers his first Budget tomorrow (Wednesday), alongside the OBR's updated economic and fiscal outlook.
Healey has signalled cost-of-living support will be "targeted and temporary" rather than universal - there's no confirmed steer yet on mainstream or high-needs school funding.
Otherwise a genuinely quiet half-term week - Sheffield schools are closed until Monday 2 November, and there's no major new national education story in the last day.
Locally, Sheffield remains one of four finalists for UK City of Culture 2029, alongside Blackpool, Milton Keynes and Wrexham.

diary.text: Sheffield schools' autumn half term continues.
Chancellor John Healey's first Budget, with the OBR's Economic and Fiscal Outlook published alongside it.
NEU's formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload closes.
UK City of Culture 2029 winner announced; Sheffield is one of four finalists.

items.body: Chancellor John Healey delivers his first Budget on Wednesday, with the Office for Budget Responsibility publishing its updated Economic and Fiscal Outlook alongside it. Healey has said living-cost support will be "targeted and temporary" rather than universal; nothing has been confirmed either way yet on further top-ups to mainstream or high-needs school funding, so treat any pre-Budget schools figures circulating this week as speculation until it's delivered.
items.action: Hold off on budget-planning assumptions until Wednesday's statement and the DfE's response to it are out.

items.lede: Sheffield in the final four for City of Culture 2029.
items.body: Sheffield is competing with Blackpool, Milton Keynes and Wrexham for the UK City of Culture 2029 title after making the shortlist; all four get at least £125,000 to develop their bids, with £10 million for the eventual winner. Council leader Fran Belbin has pointed to potential benefits for young people's career pathways and aspirations as part of the city's bid.

box.label: Jargon-buster - OBR
box.intro: Wednesday's Budget comes with an independent verdict attached.
box.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) is the UK's independent fiscal watchdog. It publishes an Economic and Fiscal Outlook alongside every Budget, checking the Chancellor's sums against the government's own borrowing and debt rules - its verdict often shapes how much room a Chancellor really has to spend.
